_note: Final country in the original 5-country candidates-only tier (after JP/KR/SA/TR). Afghanistan's unlinked nodes are mostly auto-imported international-agency statistics ABOUT Afghanistan (UNFPA, WHO, OCHA, FAO GIEWS, World Bank, UNICEF, IOM) rather than NSIA/DAB's own domestic products, so the useful evidence came from each source publisher's own page (the node's own listed url) naming its actual data/methodology origin, not from a domestic Afghan chain like Taiwan's or Korea's. Direct fetch and quote-verification of every evidence_url by the orchestrating session. 5 nodes closed with 6 edges (one, af-wheat, ties to the same new IPC node as af-humanitarian), 2 new international-standard nodes proposed (both already exist as real, independently-verifiable global bodies with no prior corpus representation), plus one bonus edge for an already-linked node (af-bop -> imf-bpm6) found along the way. 6 of 11 originally-unlinked nodes remain dropped, all genuinely thin/blocked rather than under-researched (agriculture, trade, drought, education, border-mobility deferred or no-document).

reports.title: WHO Global Health Estimates
reports.description: WHO's global health estimates programme, producing internationally comparable life-expectancy, healthy-life-expectancy, cause-of-death, and burden-of-disease estimates for all WHO member states. Cited directly on WHO's own country data portal as the source for life-expectancy statistics.

reports.title: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)
reports.publisher: IPC Global Partnership (FAO, WFP, FEWS NET and other partners)
reports.description: The international standard scale and methodology (Phase 1 Minimal through Phase 5 Catastrophe/Famine) for classifying the severity and magnitude of acute and chronic food insecurity, used by UN agencies, governments and NGOs worldwide to produce comparable food-security analyses across countries.

dependencies.basis: UNFPA's Afghanistan data page (af-population's own listed url) explicitly attributes its total-population figure to the UN Population Division: "Total population: World Population Prospects 2024 revision. United Nations Population Division, 2024." Same page also attributes life-expectancy and fertility-rate figures to the same source, confirming this is a direct-data (not merely methodological) dependency, matching the pattern already minted for sa-population -> un-wpp-methodology.

Da Afghanistan Bank's own Monthly Inflation Report (July 2021) states: "The National Statistics and Information Authority (NSIA) have brought some changes in the CPI basket in both base-year (changed to April 2015 from March 2011) and items. As a result, significant changes can be observed in the current weight and index." This corroborates, from a second, independently-fetched document, the same NSIA-supplies-the-CPI-basket relationship already minted for af-dab -> af-nsia from DAB's quarterly economic bulletin.

Fetched directly: af-exchange-rate's own listed url (dab.gov.af) resolves to a page titled "Exchange Rates | Da Afghanistan Bank", confirming the exchange-rate series this node represents is DAB's own direct publication (not a third-party compilation) — the same institution already established in the corpus as publishing af-exchange-rate's underlying data (af-dab's description: "Publishes exchange rates, inflation references and limited monetary series").

af-health's own listed url (WHO's Afghanistan country data portal) explicitly cites its life-expectancy source: "Life expectancy and health life expectancy World Health Organization, Global Health Estimates, https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/themes/mortality-and-global-health-estimates/ghe-life-expectancy-and-healthy-life-expectancy". No corpus node existed for WHO Global Health Estimates prior to this — proposed above.

af-humanitarian's own listed url (OCHA's Afghanistan page) states its food-insecurity figures directly in IPC's own phase terms: "...projected to face crisis or worse food insecurity (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification [IPC] Phase 3+), including 4.7 million experiencing emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels." No corpus node existed for the IPC classification prior to this — proposed above.

af-wheat's own listed url (FAO GIEWS Afghanistan country brief) lists IPC explicitly among the data/tools underlying the brief: "This brief was prepared using the following data/tools: FAO/GIEWS Country Cereal Balance Sheet (CCBS)... FAO/GIEWS Food Price Monitoring and Analysis (FPMA) Tool... FAO/GIEWS Earth Observation for Crop Monitoring... Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) https://www.ipcinfo.org/." The same page also states the wheat-gap figures directly in IPC phase terms (17.4 million people in IPC Phase 3+, 4.7 million in IPC Phase 4).

BONUS FIND (af-bop was already linked, not part of the 11-node unlinked set, but the evidence surfaced while researching af-exchange-rate on the same DAB site). DAB's own External Sector Statistics page titles its published balance-of-payments release explicitly with the manual it follows: "Balance of Payments Transactions (BPM6) Download" — i.e. DAB's own BOP publication is titled and filed under the IMF's Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, 6th Edition.

_dropped.why: MAIL's (Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock) own reports page (mail.gov.af/dr/reports), af-agriculture's own listed url, is a bare Dari-language navigation index (project/report category links) with no methodology or source-attribution text. No document found stating a specific data relationship to NSIA or another corpus node.

FAO GIEWS's Afghanistan brief (af-wheat's own url) names its cereal-production data source as FAO/GIEWS's own Country Cereal Balance Sheet (CCBS) system, not MAIL or NSIA directly: "the cereal supply and demand data included in this brief originates from the FAO/GIEWS Country Cereal Balance System (CCBS). The CCBS is a unique database created and continuously kept up to date by the GIEWS and Basic Foodstuffs Teams..." CCBS is not a corpus node and is a FAO-internal compiled database (a `redistributed`/`unpublishable-source`-style terminus), not a documented link to af-agriculture.

The World Bank's Afghanistan Development Update (May 2026), af-trade's own listed source document, attributes its trade tables not to NSIA or Da Afghanistan Bank but to "WB Staff calculations based on Automated System for Customs Data (ASYCUDA)" — a UNCTAD-run customs system, not a corpus node and not an Afghan government publication. No Harmonized System (HS) classification statement was found in the document either.

RE-CHECKED 2026-08-30 via browser (Chrome), since the domain is Cloudflare/edge-blocked to a direct curl/WebFetch but renders normally in a real browser. unicef.org/afghanistan/education is a static programme-description page: enrolment figures ("An estimated 3.7 million children are out-of-school in Afghanistan – 60% of them are girls") stated as UNICEF's own framing, no named source dataset, standard, or methodology (no ISCED, no UNESCO Institute for Statistics mention anywhere on the page). Followed through to data.unicef.org/country/afg/, UNICEF's own data hub for Afghanistan: its education indicators are also unattributed to any specific corpus-eligible source on the page itself (MICS is named as UNICEF's general household-survey vehicle site-wide, not stated as this page's specific input). No document found stating the relationship. Access is no longer the blocker — content is.

RE-CHECKED 2026-08-30 via browser (Chrome), since the domain is Akamai-edge-blocked to a direct curl/WebFetch but renders normally in a real browser. dtm.iom.int/afghanistan's own "About" text describes DTM's mandate and lists the humanitarian/development bodies it feeds (WFP, FAO, UNHCR, IRC, DRC, NRC, WHO, IOM's own RADA programme, the World Bank) — none of them a report node in this corpus, and none named as a citable document. The page is a landing/reports-index, not a methodology statement; no specific dataset or standard is named as af-border-mobility's own basis. No document found stating a dependency to any existing corpus node. Access is no longer the blocker — content is.

FEWS NET's Afghanistan page (af-drought's own listed url) is reachable but describes drought's role in food insecurity only narratively ("the ongoing drought's impact on food production, livelihoods and livestock... are directly driving a worsening nutrition crisis", from OCHA's page), never as a formal data-source citation with a named dataset or document. No specific quote ties af-drought's own statistics to a numbered input for af-humanitarian or af-wheat's calculations — a real causal relationship in the world, but not a documented dependency in the evidentiary sense this corpus requires.
